t.name: Mt. Jupiter Trail #809
t.description: The trail follows a long ridge line dividing the Duckabush and Dosewallips drainages before ascending to the summit of Mount Jupiter and specatular views of Puget Sound and the Olympic Mountains.

t.name: Mount Ellinor Trail #812
t.description: This trail is steep and rocky as it climbs to specatular views of Lake Cushman, Puget Sound, and the interior Olympic Mountains.

t.name: Elk Lake Trail #805
t.description: This 1.5 mile trail has both old and second growth forests and views of Jefferson Creek Drainage area. Opportunities for fishing and nature viewing at Elk Lake.

t.name: Jefferson Lake Trail #829
t.description: This 0.5 mile trail travels to Jefferson Lake, a peaceful lake that was formed during an ancient earthquake that created a rock dam at the outlet. Wildlife viewing and fishing are popular activities at this lake.

t.name: Tunnel Creek Trail #841
t.description: The trail follows South Fork Tunnel Creek for past a wooden shelter. At 3 miles the trail crosses the creek and then climbs steadily to Harrison Lake and 5050 Pass. Continue for a very steep descent to Dosewallips River for a one way trip of 7.9 miles.

t.name: Murhut Falls Trail #828
t.description: This 0.8 mile trail goes through second growth to old growth forest around Murhut Falls. In the spring rhododendrons flower along the short trail.

t.name: Lena Lake Trail #810
t.description: The popular 3.6 mile trail to Lena Lake and Lena Lake Campground is well maintained and is a moderate grade with long switchbacks.

t.name: The Brothers Trail #821
t.description: This trail enters The Brothers Wilderness and leads through a remote canyon area called the Valley of the Silent Men.

t.name: Duckabush Trail #803
t.description: This trail follows the Duckabush River into The Brothers Wilderness and enters Olympic National Park at 6.7 miles.

t.name: Duckabush River Trail
t.description: This backcountry trail follows the Duckabush River from the park boundary to O'Neil Pass.

t.name: West Fork Dosewallips River Trail
t.description: The trail begins at Dose Forks and climbs up the valley of the West Fork Dosewallips River to Anderson Pass.

t.name: Putvin Trail #813
t.description: This trail climbs steeply up the side of the Hamma Hamma River Valley before entering the national park and cresting at the Lake of the Angels.

t.name: Mt. Washington Trail
t.description: Verty steep trail leading to the top of Mount Washington. Hard to follow in places.

t.name: Jefferson Pass Trail #800
t.description: This short trail climbs at a gentle grade through mature fir and hemlock forest. The elevation is comparatively high, yet the firs are 3 feet or more in diameter, with an open understory.

t.name: Mount Ellinor Connector Trail #827.2
t.description: Trail connecting the Big Creek Loop Trail to the Mount Ellinor Trail.

t.name: Upper Big Creek Loop Trail #827.1
t.description: This trail loops around the Big Creek valley below Mount Ellinor.

t.name: Dosewallips River Road
t.description: Hike along the closed Dosewallips River Road to the former campground.

t.name: Dosewallips River Trail
t.description: The trail follows the main fork of the Dosewallips River from the Dose Ranger Station to Hayden Pass.

t.name: Lake Constance Route
t.description: Very steep and rough trail which requires the use of hands in places which takes the hiker to the alpine setting of Lake Constance.

t.name: Constance Pass Trail
t.description: This trail through many switchbacks, lifts the hiker out of the Dosewallips River Valley up to the high alpine county of Constance Pass.

t.name: Hamma Hamma Beaver Pond #815
t.description: This 0.5 mile trail is a rolling grade in a wetland pond setting. There is a bench overlooking the pond.

t.name: Living Legacy Interpretive Trail
t.description: The Living Legacy Interpretive trail is a 1.5 mile loop. The first 1/4 mile is accessible and travels along the Hamma Hamma River. Features of this section of the trail include views of the river and benches overlooking the river.

t.name: Jefferson Ridge Trail #808
t.description: This 1.6 mile trail leads to the top of the ridge through a second growth forest of Douglas-fir.
